description: Machine-readable tier scenarios for the fidelity ladder (ADR-0010, ADR-0011). Each scenario is a clinically-recognisable situation, its expected tier, and the claims the twin may and may not make in it. Loaded by tests/test_tier_scenarios.py and re-usable as documentation, demo input, or a conformance suite for any future implementation.

signal_families.caregiver_report: Structured caregiver and clinician entry. Requires no device.
signal_families.phone_ambient: Passive smartphone sensing — movement, screen interaction, call patterns, location if opted in.
signal_families.wristband: Consumer wristband — heart-rate variability, actigraphy, inertial measurement.

T0_REPORT.hardware_envelope: None beyond a device the clinician already uses.
T0_REPORT.reimbursement_fit: CPT 99483 cognitive assessment and care plan.

T1_AMBIENT.hardware_envelope: A smartphone the household already owns.
T1_AMBIENT.reimbursement_fit: GUIDE Dementia Care Management Payment; chronic care management.
T1_AMBIENT.typical_setting: Low- and middle-income deployment; community health worker workflow.

T2_PHYSIOLOGICAL.reimbursement_fit: GUIDE DCMP at higher complexity; remote therapeutic monitoring codes.

T3_NEURAL.hardware_envelope: All of T2 plus an EEG headband and the support staffing it implies.
T3_NEURAL.reimbursement_fit: None. Research and trial funding only.

scenarios.name: Memory clinic intake, no devices issued
scenarios.narrative: A person is seen in a memory clinic. A care plan is written and the caregiver completes a burden questionnaire. Nothing is worn home.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The most common real starting state. A twin must be useful here or it is not deployable at scale.

scenarios.name: Community health worker deployment, phone only
scenarios.narrative: A community health worker enrols a household with a shared smartphone. No wearable is available or affordable.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The configuration that reaches the ~71% of people with dementia projected to live in LMICs by 2050. Deviation from personal baseline is genuinely useful here; conversion risk is not supportable.

scenarios.name: Standard home deployment
scenarios.narrative: Phone plus consumer wristband, worn consistently. No neural sensing.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The intended default product. Everything the clinician-facing surface needs, with no neural hardware.

scenarios.name: Full research configuration
scenarios.narrative: Academic centre, all sensing present, participant trained and supported.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The only configuration in which the Memory Anchoring Pipeline may run at all.

scenarios.name: Headband removed mid-day
scenarios.narrative: A participant in the full configuration takes the headband off after lunch. Everything else keeps reporting.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The modal real-world event. The twin must degrade to T2 and keep working, not continue asserting T3 claims against stale neural data.

scenarios.name: Wristband battery flat overnight
scenarios.why_it_matters: Conversion-risk scoring must suspend, not silently continue on a thinner signal set.

scenarios.name: Headband present but no phone or wristband
scenarios.narrative: A misconfigured or partially-provisioned deployment: neural hardware arrives, supporting devices do not.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Tiers are contiguous. Neural data without behavioural or physiological context is exactly what the MAP must not act on, so this is T0 rather than T3.

scenarios.name: Wristband without a phone to relay it
scenarios.narrative: A wristband is issued but the household has no smartphone.
scenarios.why_it_matters: An unreachable sensor is not a sensor. Skipping levels would let a sparse configuration claim fidelity its context cannot justify.

scenarios.name: No signals at all
scenarios.narrative: A record exists but nothing has ever reported, including caregiver entry.
scenarios.why_it_matters: T0 is the floor, but a twin at the floor with nothing beneath it still may not make claims. Even care-plan support requires the caregiver report.

scenarios.name: Unrecognised device in the signal set
scenarios.narrative: A device integration reports a signal family the twin does not know about.
scenarios.why_it_matters: A typo in an integration must surface as an explained tier, not as a mysteriously absent alert.

scenarios.name: Signal names with inconsistent casing and whitespace
scenarios.narrative: An upstream system sends signal names in mixed case with padding.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Normalisation failure would silently downgrade a fully-provisioned patient.

scenarios.name: Fidelity restored when the headband goes back on
scenarios.narrative: The participant from S05 puts the headband back on the following morning.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Recovery must be automatic and must not emit a downgrade note. Tier is derived per evaluation, so nothing needs re-enrolling.
